Republican Governor [[Bruce Rauner]] ran for reelection to a second term in office, but was defeated by Democratic nominee [[JB Pritzker]]. This is the most recent Illinois gubernatorial contest in which an incumbent was defeated and the last time the governorship of Illinois changed partisan control. Rauner oversaw a historic [[Illinois budget impasse|budget crisis]] as governor that severely affected his popularity.{{cite news |last1=Korecki |first1=Natasha |title=How Illinois became America's failed state |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/06/10/illinois-debt-deficit-budget-election-239384 |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=POLITICO |date=June 10, 2017}} His approval rating declined to just 36% in 2017, and he was widely viewed as the most vulnerable incumbent governor in the country.{{cite news |last1=Clauss |first1=Hunter |title=Poll: Rauner’s Disapproval Rating Almost Doubles Since 2015 |url=https://www.wbez.org/chicago/2017/03/15/poll-rauners-disapproval-rating-almost-doubles-since-2015 |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=WBEZ Chicago |date=March 15, 2017}}{{cite news |last1=Kraushaar |first1=Josh |title=Why Bruce Rauner Is the Most Vulnerable Governor |url=https://www.nationaljournal.com/s/665672/why-bruce-rauner-is-most-vulnerable-governor/ |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=National Journal |date=March 25, 2018}} Rauner struggled to galvanize conservatives after making several policy concessions to Democrats and was nearly ousted in the Republican primary by state senator [[Jeanne Ives]].{{cite news |last1=Baichwal |first1=Ravi |last2=Elgas |first2=Rob |title=Illinois Primary 2018: Bruce Rauner wins tight race against Jeanne Ives for GOP nomination |url=https://abc7chicago.com/post/bruce-rauner-wins-tight-race-against-jeanne-ives-for-gop-nomination/3239443/ |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=ABC7 Chicago |date=March 21, 2018}} By October 2018, ''The Cook Political Report'' assessed that "there is no path to victory for Rauner."{{cite news |last1=Duffy |first1=Jennifer |title=Governors: Rating Changes Four States |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/governors/governors-overview/governors-rating-changes-four-states |access-date=April 17, 2026 |work=The Cook Political Report |date=October 5, 2018}} Pritzker ultimately defeated Rauner by nearly 16 points, the largest gubernatorial victory in Illinois since [[Jim Edgar]]'s [[1994 Illinois gubernatorial election|1994 reelection]]. Rauner's loss was the widest margin of defeat for any incumbent governor since [[Ernie Fletcher]] of [[Kentucky]] was ousted in [[2007 Kentucky gubernatorial election|2007]]. This was one of seven governorships Democrats flipped during the [[2018 United States gubernatorial elections|2018 cycle]]. Rauner's 38.8% of the vote was the worst performance for an incumbent Illinois governor since [[1912 Illinois gubernatorial election|1912]]; he also received the lowest percentage of the vote for a Republican since 1912. With Pritzker winning by a margin of 15.7%, this was the biggest gubernatorial margin of victory for a Democrat since [[1932 Illinois gubernatorial election|1932]]. He was the first Democrat to carry DuPage County since 1932, Kane and Kendall counties since [[1852 Illinois gubernatorial election|1852]], and DeKalb County since 1972. ==Background== The primaries and general elections coincided with those for federal [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois|congressional races]] and those for other state offices.
